sections.skill: Compute cost per item and compare it with price

questions.prompt: A batch of 50 bracelets uses 75 dollars of beads and string. What is the cost per bracelet?
questions.intro: COST PER ITEM (unit cost) is what it costs you to make or buy one item. If a batch of 40 cookies uses 20 dollars of ingredients and 4 dollars of bags, the cost per cookie is (20 + 4) / 40 = 0.60 dollars. PRICE is what the customer pays. The difference, price minus cost per item, is what each sale contributes toward fixed costs and profit. A price below the cost per item loses money on every sale. Include everything the item uses, such as packaging and labels, not just the main material.

questions.prompt: 24 dollars for 8 items. What is the cost per item?
questions.intro: To find the cost of one item from a batch, add up everything the batch cost, then divide by the number of items. Example: 30 dollars for 12 items: 30 / 12 = 2.50 dollars each. Check by multiplying back: 2.50 x 12 = 30. If the answer is bigger than the total, you probably divided the wrong way.
